sections.title: New in V54: Global interface refinement
items: The walk-through remains temporarily disabled. Use the Help button above Menu for page-specific guidance.
Use Edit Home to customise the dashboard. Project Settings and its General, Project Info, Production Contacts, Lighting Vendor, Logos and Exports sections are available in the sidebar beneath Home.

Every Job Type now offers Festival, Europe and US Theatres/Sheds. Use Add New Contact in Production Contacts to enter Job Title and Name. Set visibility and use Re-order to drag contacts or move them with Up/Down buttons.

Lighting Vendor retains saved contacts without add-contact buttons. The Logos preview uses the current PDF logo styles; Exports shows a full-width, normal-scale first-page header preview without a footer directly below First-page Header.

Use the sidebar for Patch, imported comparison sheets and Universe Detail. Add Fixtures and Unpatch Fixture sit on the toolbar left; Export stays on the right. Hidden columns survive reloads and remaining columns expand with priority for Type, Mode and wrapped text.
Merge Universe & Address has its own control beside the filters. New settings use a spaced dot, for example 1 . 101. Existing saved separators remain unchanged.

Universe Detail keeps its universe selectors and Move Selected/Move All actions. Hover or focus a fixture footprint to highlight every channel it uses. The page title stays unchanged when selecting a universe.
Power and Fan Outs use sidebar navigation. Fan Outs inherits Power Calcs Full Name/Short Name selection and uses the same solid internal table borders.

sections.title: New in V53: Navigation and page help
items: The walk-through is temporarily disabled. Use the page-specific Help button above Menu; this guide is retained for future use.
Select a page in the left sidebar. Selecting another page group closes the previous group in both expanded and compact navigation. The active sub-page is highlighted.
Use the collapse/expand control beside the app logo to switch between full labels and the compact icon rail. Menu at the bottom opens project actions; it does not resize the sidebar.

In compact navigation, the active group shows its sub-page icons. Hover or focus a sub-page for its name. Hover an inactive group for its destinations; Home omits its own name. A single patch sheet does not repeat the Patch shortcut.
Open Home → Project Settings to edit project information, contacts, logos and export defaults. Project Settings is no longer in Menu.
Press the circled question-mark Help button above Menu for guidance about the current page. Close the dialog with its close button, Escape or its backdrop.
Individual loom cards start collapsed. Click a loom heading to open or close it. Open-card preferences survive page switching and reloads in this browser without changing project data.
On narrow screens, open navigation with the button above the page header. Selecting a page closes the drawer. Escape or clicking outside also closes it.
Sidebar size is remembered in this browser. Navigation and loom disclosure preferences do not change PDF layouts.

sections.title: New in V51: Fixture Patch and Universe Detail
items: Open Universe Detail under Fixture Patch, or select a universe from Home. This view edits the Master Patch.
Select Patched Fixtures to highlight their footprints. Use Shift for a range or Select All, then Move Selected to Universe. Starting addresses are retained.
Drag a patched footprint to propose an address. Green indicates a valid destination; red displays a conflict or overflow. Confirm in the address-review dialogue; Cancel leaves the patch unchanged.

The circular Fixture Patch menu contains Import, Fixture Summary, Position Summary and Delete Patch. Export stays in the toolbar. Oops restores recent patch changes; column visibility uses selection buttons.

PDF column buttons affect only the open export session. Empty columns remain omitted per fixture type. Additional-page switches sit between Hidden Columns and PDF Logos; the summary quantity header reads Qty.

sections.title: New in V50: Device Config
items: Device Config tables sort independently within each Location group and keep device ports attached to their parent.
Port Configuration is a dedicated Network sub-tab with one tab per compatible DMX-node device and save-on-switch editing.
Device Config Export opens every tree, repeats the VLAN settings grid on each page and provides separate preview collapse and row-inclusion controls.
Global Subnet opens above the page as a viewport-level panel, while all Device Config Location cells use the shared Position colour presentation.

sections.title: New in V49: Unified Control
items: Control now shows Consoles first and NPUs second in one page, with both sections visible in Card View and Table View.
The shared Control toolbar adds either device type and expands or collapses every Console and NPU parent row.
Control Table View uses collapsible Device Config-style location groups, independent sorting and spreadsheet keyboard, selection, copy, paste and drag-fill controls.
Matching Control Location cells use Position Summary colours and the same solid or striped presentation as Power Position cells.
Card position names use the Project Font while card controls retain the App Font.

sections.title: New in V48: Browser-width layouts
items: Every live page fits the space between the sidebar and the right edge, with 10px header and application-shell padding. There is no fixed page-width wrapper.
Fixture Patch and Power Calcs tables scale to fill the available sheet width.
Device Config distributes its columns across the sheet and scales only below its readable minimum.
Rack Layout and label layouts scale as complete workspaces while preserving their internal proportions.
Home cards and application controls reflow without changing their control sizes, while print and PDF output keep their document geometry.

sections.title: Network and Errors
items: Network opens Device Config, which is the shared place to review and edit network devices, interfaces, addresses, subnets and VLAN assignments.

Press Errors to the right of the Tour Logo to review recent active issues. The badge counts active errors. New errors pulse red until acknowledged; Show All Errors opens the grouped review page. Report Issue is in Menu.
Use Active and Ignored to review errors by page. Select individual errors or Select All within a group, then use Ignore Errors or Restore Errors.
Select an affected record to reveal its field. The app checks duplicate or invalid IP addresses, fixture patch data and Power supply warnings.
Corrected errors disappear. An ignored error becomes Active if the same problem is corrected and later returns.

sections.title: Recommended Workflow
items: Open Home → Project Settings and enter the project name, dates, production details, logos, general defaults and export defaults.

In Power, use + Distro to set its name, catalogue type, phase mapping, input connector, Supply feed source, P/Lock adaptor and RCBO. Add supported Aux and 3ø outputs. Catalogue settings provide the Socapex count and input rating; new Distros use the project voltage.
Build the Fixture Patch by adding fixtures from the library or importing CSV, Excel, XLSM, or MVR data.

Open the full-page Positions workspace from Home Position Summary or Fixture Patch to create positions and assign up to three colours. Position names and colours are shared with the patch, power calculations, labels, Control, Rack Layout and Device Config.
Open Power and assign distros to supplies. Enter fixture IDs to link each way to Fixture Patch data, then check phase totals, RCBO warnings, Aux outlets, and the PDF preview.

Use Control to add consoles and NPUs, including roles, locations, parameters, protocols, IP addresses, DMX ports, and reference images. Consoles and NPUs appear together in separate Control sections; choose Card View or Table View for the required workflow. Add switches, nodes and other network-capable hardware through Rack Layout or Device Config.
Open Rack Layout to create racks, set their U size and depth, and place project or library devices from the Front or Rear view. Use Side view to inspect device depths and cable clearance.
Open Network → Device Config to review the synchronized device tree, expand individual ports, and edit patch, IP, subnet, protocol, direction, VLAN, and notes data.
Use Global Subnet in Device Config to set the default subnet for new devices and apply it to existing network interfaces when required.
Review the Fan Outs page generated from Power and export the required Fan Out paperwork.
Use Labels to complete Front RCBO Labels, Rear Labels, and Table View, then preview and export the required label pages.
Review Revisions from the Actions menu or Home card, then download the Lampy project file so the editable project can be reopened later.

sections.title: Fixture Patch, GDTF, and MVR
items: The fixture library shows GDTF ✅ only when a repository file has a fully matched manufacturer, fixture type, mode, and channel count. GDTF ❌ means an exact match is not currently available.
Use Import to load CSV, Excel, XLSM, or MVR files. Imported comparison sheets in the sidebar highlight new, removed, and changed patch data before it is merged into the master patch.
Fixture Patch Export provides Output Options, independent column controls and PDF Logos. Show Fixture Summary and Show Patch Revision Notes sit in their own card between Hidden Columns and PDF Logos.
MVR export checks fixture IDs, DMX addresses, modes, duplicate ranges, and GDTF availability before building the file.
V33 imports supported MVR 1.5 and 1.6 patch data, including fixture positions, layers, classes, UUID metadata, and embedded GDTF filenames with or without the .gdtf extension.
MVR export uses standards-formatted UUIDs and DMX addresses, creates one layer per Lampy fixture position, and embeds the exact matched GDTF file and mode.

Use Add GDTF Files in Fixture Patch Export when a repository match is unavailable. Manual upload remains a fallback and produces a report for matches, revisions, duplicates, missing fixtures, errors, and oversized files.

sections.title: Control, Device Config and Rack Layout
items: Consoles and NPUs added in Control appear automatically in Device Config. Control displays Consoles and NPUs together as separate sections, including empty sections with their add action.
Control groups consoles and NPUs by project position. Consoles are ordered Master, Backup, unassigned, then by name; NPUs remain sorted by name.

Choose Card View for device summary cards or Table View for Device Config-style editing, expandable ports, keyboard navigation, copy and paste, selection, and vertical drag-fill. The last Control view is remembered by the browser.

Device names, locations, roles, modes, software, parameters, IP addresses, port settings, protocols, VLANs and notes remain linked between Control, Device Config and Rack Layout. Multi-network-port DMX Nodes show a separate front/rear VLAN field for each physical network port in Rack Layout. Rack position, mounting face and physical dimensions remain controlled by Rack Layout.
Device Config branches are collapsed by default. Expand a device to see its Ethernet, fibre, XLR-5 DMX, and supported secondary-interface records.
Use arrow keys, Enter, Shift+Enter, Tab, and Shift+Tab to move through Device Config. Copy, paste, select ranges, or drag the fill handle vertically through compatible cells.
Rack Layout provides Front, Side, and Rear views. Front and Rear are mounting faces; Side is a depth overview where existing devices can still be moved vertically.
New racks default to 700 mm deep. Rack Depth can be edited, but every device must retain at least 100 mm of space behind it for cabling.
Front- and rear-mounted devices may share a U only when their combined depths plus the 100 mm cable space fit inside the rack.
Use Simple view for names and device types, or Detailed view for the front and rear line images supplied by the device library.

Use Port Configuration on supported DMX Nodes to assign universes, directions, names, and project positions. Quick Config fills every port consecutively, while selected-port controls adjust existing universe values by 1, 5 or 10. Assigned position colours appear on mapped DMX sockets in Detailed Rack Layout views.
Use + Device to add and configure network equipment from Device Config. Reference-library rack hardware can also be added from Rack Layout.
Global Subnet can automatically supply the subnet for new devices. Manually changing an interface subnet excludes it from later global updates until Apply to all Devices is used.
Each device can contain two IP addresses. Subnet and VLAN values are stored per interface, while the device name, location, and notes remain shared.
VLAN Setup uses the Generic, Luminex or Pathway template selected for the project. Names and colours remain editable, and device VLAN assignments remain unchanged when a template is loaded.
A Notes value of SPARE uses the project-wide SPARE styling automatically.

sections.title: Power
items: Fixture IDs link Power to Fixture Patch names, watts, positions, and position colours. Duplicate fixture IDs are highlighted.
Enter multiple IDs in one Fix ID cell with &, +, comma, /, > or a spaced hyphen. IDs remain individually validated and included in load totals.

Use the arrow keys, Enter, Shift+Enter, Tab, and Shift+Tab to move between editable Power Calcs cells. Drag the selected cell's blue fill handle vertically to copy a value through a compatible column.
Choose Full Name or Short Name independently for the Power display.
Select a 16 Amp or 10 Amp RCBO in each distro settings. A way is warned above 15.01 A for a 16 Amp RCBO or above 9.01 A for a 10 Amp RCBO.

Add Aux outlets three at a time. Each connector-labelled group follows the selected Distro phase mapping. Only enabled Aux outlets contribute to power calculations. Configured 3ø Outputs appear separately.
Use Power Calcs for detailed assignments, Fan Outs for display-only Socapex paperwork, and Phase Totals when it is available for supply and connected-distro review.
Power and Fan Outs PDFs start each Distro on a new page. Power includes linked phase summaries and omits the final Totals page when the project has exactly one Supply.

sections.title: Labels
items: Before labels are generated, Labels opens Table View. Table View remains live and editable whether or not labels have been generated.
Press Generate Labels to create Front RCBO Labels and Rear Labels from current Power data. The button becomes Update Labels after generation.
Power changes do not alter generated label previews. Press Update Labels when you want the previews and Labels export to use the latest Power data.
Each generated distro heading records its generation date and time. Socapex, Aux, and Output labels support label formatting and colour controls.
Use Label Settings and Label Format before exporting. Labels export becomes available after labels are generated.

sections.title: Revisions and Saving
items: Changes to Project Info, Fixture Patch, Power, Control, distro labels, output settings and GDTF metadata create revision notes in the latest working version.
Use Bump Version Number to increment the project version and add the current date. Notes can be edited, removed, or moved to another version.
Similar automatic changes are grouped into a short client-facing summary. Use Download Change Log when the detailed activity log is needed.
The browser saves a working copy locally, but Download Project is the portable backup. Use Open Project to continue from a saved Lampy project file.

sections.title: Useful Tips
items: The Home tab provides clickable totals for Fixtures, Universes, Consoles, parameters, Distros, Socapexes, and Data Racks. These open the relevant project page directly.

Use Edit Home to reorder, resize, hide, restore, or collapse dashboard cards. Changes are stored with the current project; Set as Browser Default applies the chosen layout to future and legacy projects.

Use Edit at the top of Position Summary to open the Positions workspace. Renaming a position updates linked fixtures and devices; removing one clears it from affected project records after confirmation.
Opening Universes from Home displays a full-page Universe Detail view with one tab per patched universe. Select Home in the sidebar when finished.
In compact navigation, hover or focus an inactive page group to see its destinations. Active-group sub-pages appear directly in the sidebar and show only their own name on hover.
Fixture group title lines always use the full fixture name. Full Name and Short Name options affect supported table cells and labels only.
Use the Fixture Patch lock before editing rows, and watch for duplicate fixture IDs or overlapping DMX addresses. Show/Hide Columns is available beside Clear Filters in the Filter & Sort controls.
Supply cards can be collapsed after setup to keep Power tidy.
Manage project logos in Home → Project Settings → Logos; vendor controls are also available in Lighting Vendor. Logos can be included in supported exports.
All project, GDTF, and MVR processing is local to the browser. Lampy Paperwork does not import grandMA3 .show files or modify grandMA3 system libraries.
Use Menu → Report Issue for bugs, missing fixture requests or feature suggestions.
